lesson.title: Inside the CPU: ALU, CU and Von Neumann Architecture

images.alt: Main memory connected to the CPU, showing the control unit and arithmetic logic unit.
Instructions and data stored together in main memory for the CPU to fetch.

questions.prompt: Which unit performs arithmetic and logical operations?
In Von Neumann architecture, where are instructions and data stored?
Write the three-letter abbreviation for the control unit.
Write the three-letter abbreviation for the arithmetic logic unit.
Describe the different roles of the ALU and CU when the CPU processes an instruction.
questions.model_answer: The ALU performs arithmetic or logical operations. The CU decodes/coordinates instructions and sends control signals.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: The ALU performs arithmetic or logical operations.
1: The CU decodes/coordinates instructions and sends control signals.
questions.student_guidance:
Think about the operations one unit carries out on values.
Think about how the other unit interprets instructions and directs components.

questions.prompt: Explain why main memory is needed when a CPU runs a program that processes data.
questions.model_answer: Main memory holds program instructions for the CPU to fetch. Main memory also holds data the program uses or processes.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: Main memory holds program instructions for the CPU to fetch.
1: Main memory also holds data the program uses or processes.
questions.student_guidance:
Consider where the CPU obtains the program's next instruction.
Consider where values used by that program are held while it runs.
